title: LLM-based NPCs in Video Games: A Systematic Mapping Study
abstract: arXiv:2611.05427v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: For decades, non-player characters (NPCs) have been driven by rule-based systems whose personalities and interactions are scripted before release. Large language models (LLMs) promise NPCs that converse openly, adapt to new situations, and behave in ways developers did not fully author, prompting a wave of research and commercial experimentation. Yet the field lacks a unified picture of what has been built, how well it works, and at what cost. We address this gap with a systematic mapping study of 377 papers from the academic literature, yielding 42 papers analysed against a main research question and ten sub-questions across four thematic axes. translated_title: 基于大语言模型的游戏非玩家角色（NPC）：一项系统性映射研究
translated_abstract: 几十年来，非玩家角色（NPC）一直由基于规则的系统驱动，其个性和互动在游戏发布前就被预先编写好。大语言模型（LLM）有望使NPC能够进行开放式对话、适应新情况，并表现出开发者未完全预设的行为，这引发了一波研究和商业实验的浪潮。然而，该领域目前缺乏一个统一的图景，来展示已经构建了什么、效果如何以及代价是什么。我们通过对学术文献中377篇论文的系统性映射研究来弥补这一空白，最终筛选出42篇论文，围绕一个主要研究问题和十个子问题、横跨四个主题维度进行分析。我们首次提供了组件采用率、延迟、安全覆盖和可复现性的量化刻画：短期记忆和世界状态接地已接近普及（60%和69%），而长期记忆（31%）、反思（38%）和检索增强生成（14%）仍然……
tldr: 该论文通过对42篇相关文献的系统性映射研究，首次从组件采用率、延迟、安全覆盖和可复现性四个维度对基于大语言模型的游戏NPC领域进行了量化刻画。
en_tdlr: This paper conducts a systematic mapping study of 42 papers on LLM-based NPCs in video games, providing the first quantitative characterization of component adoption, latency, safety coverage, and reproducibility in this emerging field.
